questions.text: Which standard is harmonised for websites and mobile applications under the Web Accessibility Directive?
Has any harmonised standard been cited under the European Accessibility Act, and what is the status of EN 301 549?
What does WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8 require?
How should the target-size criterion be described in guidance?

claims.statement: EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03) is the harmonised standard for websites and mobile applications under Directive (EU) 2016/2102, the Web Accessibility Directive.
claims.locator: Title of the decision; annex entry for EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03)

claims.statement: As of August 2026 no harmonised standard had been cited in the Official Journal in support of Directive (EU) 2019/882, the European Accessibility Act.
claims.resolution: C5 has no source. C2 stands as REPORTED until the Official Journal index is read (C7).

claims.statement: EN 301 549 V4.1.1, which incorporates WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA, was published on 2 September 2026 under standardisation request M/587.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is Level AA and has five exceptions: spacing, equivalent, inline, user agent control and essential.
claims.locator: Success criterion text at the top of the page

claims.statement: SC 2.5.8 has been legally required under the European Accessibility Act since June 2025.
claims.resolution: Inherited sentence of unknown origin from an earlier skill file. Not supported by anything opened. Not used.

claims.statement: Do not describe SC 2.5.8, or any pixel size, as an EU legal requirement. Describe it as the WCAG 2.2 Level AA criterion.
Whether the Official Journal now cites any standard under Directive (EU) 2019/882: the Official Journal index and the ETSI text were not read.

assessments.judgement: Describe SC 2.5.8 as the WCAG 2.2 Level AA criterion and not as an EU legal requirement. The only harmonised standard established in this ledger is EN 301 549 V3.2.1 under the Web Accessibility Directive, and no standard is reported as cited under the European Accessibility Act.
assessments.confidence_reason: It rests on one REPORTED claim (C2) from a secondary source whose address was not kept, and the Official Journal index was not read (C7).
